phase3_findings.description: run_memory_call in src/sqllens/memory/store.py (lines 99-116) accepts any callable, including generator and async def functions; for those the worker only builds a generator or coroutine object and the real store reads run later on the event loop. No current caller passes one, and the type checker cannot catch it.

docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md line 119 (and 127) says input validation stays on the event loop, but list_memories' limit check (admin.py 162-163) runs inside the function passed to run_memory_call, on the memory worker; the test checks only add_memories' per-item SqlPair validation.
The module docstring of tests/unit/test_memory_event_loop.py (lines 9-10) repeats the over-broad claim that input validation stays on the loop.

The worker comment in src/sqllens/memory/store.py (lines 70-74) names 'the store's own executor' (MemoryStore has none; it is ChromaAgentMemory's) and gives a test-only reason (object.__new__) for the module-level worker instead of the real one: the import tool's store and admin_store are separate instances (server.py 412, 501) whose calls must never overlap.

docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md line 119: 'the store's own two-thread executor' should name ChromaAgentMemory, and 'last_skipped_rows is shared by every caller' holds only for callers of one MemoryStore instance.

docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md line 120 says a call cancelled while queued never runs; asyncio.wrap_future cancels the concurrent future via a call_soon callback one loop iteration later, so the worker can start the item in that window and run it to completion (the done callback still logs it).

The run_memory_call docstring in src/sqllens/memory/store.py (lines 102-103) says a caller cancelled before its call starts drops it; the same one-iteration window lets a queued call start and complete.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (seven Suggestions, no checklist failure)
The PR is ready to merge: every checklist item passed, and the reviewers raised only Suggestions, which sit below the `critical` verdict threshold.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings remain below the threshold → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (7)

<details><summary>7 items</summary>

1. `run_memory_call` in `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` (lines 99-116) accepts any callable, including a generator function or an `async def` function. For such a callable the worker only builds a generator or coroutine object, and the real store reads then run on the event loop when the caller iterates or awaits it. No current caller passes one, and the type checker cannot catch it. (raised by 1/4 agents)
2. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 119 (and line 127) says input validation stays on the event loop. `list_memories`' `limit` check (`src/sqllens/memory/admin.py` lines 162-163) runs inside the function passed to `run_memory_call`, so it runs on the memory worker. The unit test checks only `add_memories`' per-item validation (`admin.SqlPair`). (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: prose only, no output or branch changes if corrected; git grep of .sh/.py/.jq/.yml/.toml/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/.prflow/skill-extensions/.github for the doc path found only a pointer comment in src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sql_threads.py:33, no behavior reader; internal doc page nothing publishes -->
3. The module docstring of `tests/unit/test_memory_event_loop.py` (lines 9-10) repeats the claim that input validation stays on the loop, which the `limit` check does not follow. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: test docstring, no tool or agent reads it for behavior; never printed outside the repository -->
4. The worker comment in `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` (lines 70-74) names "the store's own executor", but `MemoryStore` has none; the two-thread executor belongs to `ChromaAgentMemory`. It also gives a test-only reason (`object.__new__`) for the module-level worker. The reason that matters is that the import tool's store and `admin_store` are separate instances (`server.py` lines 412 and 501) whose calls must still never overlap. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: code comment, no directive or marker; correcting it changes no output; comment is never printed -->
5. In `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 119, "the store's own two-thread executor" should name `ChromaAgentMemory`. "`last_skipped_rows` is shared by every caller" holds only for callers of one `MemoryStore` instance, because the import tool and the admin tools hold different instances. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: same search as item 2; internal doc page, no behavior reader -->
6. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 120 says "A call cancelled while it waits in the queue never runs". `asyncio.wrap_future` calls `cancel()` on the concurrent future through a `call_soon` callback, one loop iteration later. If the worker picks up the item in that window, the call runs to completion. The done callback still logs the outcome, so behavior stays correct. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: same search as item 2; the claim describes timing, and correcting it changes no output or branch -->
7. The `run_memory_call` docstring in `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` (lines 102-103) makes the same claim ("A caller cancelled before its call starts drops it"). The same one-iteration window applies. (raised by 1/4 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: docstring of an internal helper, not printed as --help or to any user; no tool reads it -->

</details>

[src/sqllens/memory/store.py:110]
  - VC-2: When the awaiting task is cancelled, asyncio's wrap_future chaining calls cancel() on the concurrent future: a call still queued is cancelled and never runs (the done callback sees future.cancelled() and logs nothing), a running call cannot be cancelled and completes on the worker, and a done callback added to an already-finished future runs immediately in the calling thread; each outcome is handled by _log_call_after_cancel. [src/sqllens/memory/store.py:113]
  - VC-3: _log_call_after_cancel logs nothing for a cancelled future, INFO naming the function for a successful one, and WARNING with exc_info set to the exception instance (which the logging module renders as a traceback) for a failed one. [src/sqllens/memory/store.py:87]

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No call to a synchronous (non-`async`) `MemoryStore` method made by an MCP tool registered under `memory.allow_admin_tools` or `memory.allow_import` runs on the event-loop thread. A test records the thread each such call runs on, for every one of those tools, and asserts it is not the thread running the event loop.
- [ ] While a memory tool's store call is held open, `GET /healthz` on the same HTTP server returns 200 within 2 seconds, measured by a 2-second httpx request timeout as in `tests/integration/test_slow_agent_run_responsiveness.py`. Once released, the held tool call returns its normal, non-error result.
- [ ] Within one server process, synchronous (non-`async`) `MemoryStore` method calls made for two different calls of those MCP tools are never in progress at the same time. This holds even when the tool call that started one is cancelled while it runs: the next such call starts only after the cancelled call's store work returns.
- [ ] For the same store contents and arguments, with no write other than the call's own overlapping it and no cancellation of the call, each of those MCP tools returns the same result as before the change, including each `isError` result and message. That covers, at minimum, a memory that is not found, a corrupt store, invalid input, a lossy export, an add or import with failed items, and a generic store failure. A `list_memories` call whose store reads a managed write (a write inside `CollectionState.writing()`) overlaps returns an `isError` result whose text contains `Memory store changed during listing; retry the request.` and never a partial listing. The existing memory tool tests pass without changes to their assertions.
- [ ] The CLI `import-memory` command reports the same saved, duplicate and error counts and exit status as before for the same store and bundle, including with `--clear` and `--dry-run`.
- [ ] The change leaves `add_memories`' per-item validation, `import_memory`'s parsing of its bundle JSON, `import_bundle`'s per-item de-duplication check of the incoming items, and each handler's final `json.dumps` of the object its `memory.admin` function returns running on the event loop.
